summary: The VerifyLeader repeat ran clean and reproduced both directions of that pair. In the trigger case, with five members, three voters and only one voter reachable while both non-voters answered, the verification succeeded in 0 ms; the successor then committed a different value and was elected at 2330 ms, the old leader had become a follower holding the new value by the time it was measured, and its later verification failed with 'node is not the leader'. In the control, with the non-voters cut as well, the same verification failed after 1005 ms with 'leadership lost while committing log' and the successor was elected at 2676 ms. Neither run served a verified read from stale data, so the bound the account already records is unchanged, and the explanation that non-voter stream acknowledgements complete a voter quorum in this shape no longer rests on a single execution of either case. I appended the parsed events for both cases to the rationale, added the receipt to the execution set alongside the two earlier runs, and extended the joint history to note that this is a repeat of the same experiment from retained inputs. All six counterevidence items, both recorded limitations, both gap answers and the two knowledge uses at revisions 8 and 6 are carried forward unchanged, and the conclusion stays explained with the scoped defect asserted.
